filename: Physics-Guided Recurrent Graph Model for Predicting Flow and Temperature in River Networks.pdf
title: Physics-Guided Recurrent Graph Model for Predicting Flow and Temperature in River Networks
testbed_rationale: Focuses on regional river network streamflow and water temperature prediction, not subgrid physical parameterization for Earth System Models.
pain_points: Severe data sparsity in river networks where most segments have few or no observations.
Order-of-magnitude scale variations across river segments (e.g., high flow vs. low headwater flow) causes global ML losses (MSE) to focus on high-flow segments while neglecting low-flow segments.
Physics-based models (PRMS-SNTemp) involve numerous interacting parameters (84 parameters), making manual/expert calibration extremely slow and computationally intensive.
Standard GCN latent embeddings learned purely data-driven lack physical interpretation and overfit when trained on sparse observation sets.
extraction_notes: The paper uses simulation pre-training to guide graph representations (PGRGrN) and a segment-wise contrastive loss to regularize predictions across varying river sizes.
